names.note: Read out of saint.gr's line for 17 Οκτωβρίου, «Άγιοι Κοσμάς, Δαμιανός, Λεόντιος, Άνθιμος και Ευπρέπιος οι Ανάργυροι», with the rank word left off; the page's own heading for this one is «Αγιος Ευπρεπιος ο Αναργυρος». The company's own name as the page gives it is «οι Ανάργυροι», the Unmercenaries, and «από την Αραβία», from Arabia; the English display name carries the province because the rank is in `types`.
The second form the page prints for him, in the account under all five names, «Ευπρέπιος (ή Eυτρόπιος)», and again in the epigram he shares with Anthimus.

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 17ης Οκτωβρίου — «Άγιοι Κοσμάς, Δαμιανός, Λεόντιος, Άνθιμος και Ευπρέπιος οι Ανάργυροι»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 17 Οκτωβρίου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing, and gives each of the five a heading of its own — his is «Αγιος Ευπρεπιος ο Αναργυρος» — with a separate epigram for Cosmas and Damian, for Leontius and for Anthimus and Euprepius, so this is a synaxis that enumerates its members and is five folders and not one. What it says it says once, under all five names: they were brothers of one another in the flesh and in the spirit, from **Arabia**; devout, all five, moved by the same divine zeal and the same love of man, who did many good works by their physician's art and drew many to the Christian faith; denounced for it and arrested in the persecution under Diocletian, **in Lycia, by Lysias the governor at Aegae**; and beheaded after many tortures. **This is the Arabian pair, and the corpus does not hold them.** It holds `cosmas-of-rome` and `damian-of-rome` on 1 July and `cosmas-of-asia` and `damian-of-asia` on 1 November — the Roman pair and the Asian pair — and the tradition keeps three pairs of unmercenary physicians of these names on three days. Checked folder by folder against every Cosmas and every Damian in `saints/`: none of them is of Arabia and none stands on 17/10 in any calendar. The page gives no year, only «κατά τον επί Διοκλητιανού διωγμό», so there is no `dates` object; Arabia, Lycia and Aegae are named and `locations` is left out as elsewhere on this reader's days. No hymn on the page. **Display names take Arabia and not «ο Ανάργυρος»**, because `unmercenary` is in `types` and `lib/honorific.js` would compose the rank twice. The corpus's `euprepius-the-confessor-disciple-of-maximus`, kept on 20 September, is another man. No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence on the life page.
